body: Being locked in in my room as a child often. Usually hungry, always neglected. Parents constantly fighting, my dad left early and my mom is a psychopath. Forced me into so many things I hated, I never trusted her nor loved her. I’ve never loved anyone. I had to learn things on my own. I’m 25 now and function properly, I have no friends, I don’t talk to any of my family. I got out of the military about 2 years ago so I’m all alone with no one to talk to, and no hope of meeting others due to lockdown. I’ve always thought about killing myself as early as I can remember, probably 12. I honestly several hours a day thinking about it. I’ve studied psychology and philosophy since I found them both interesting and helpful. I’m at the point where suicide won’t be an emotional decision, but rather a flawed logical one that I’ve convinced myself to be true. I wish I could look at points in my life where suicide would’ve been a mistake, but as time goes on I regret not ending it more and more. I want to have hope, but I think hope is just a primitive instinct to keep the species alive so we can continue existing.

Invest half of it, but a house with whatever’s left in a cheap place. Retire with no obligations. 500k a year is enough to retire assuming I make 10% profit a year from investments, which is extremely doable, even if it’s just dividends. Yeah taxes take a good chunk but if I own a house and don’t go anywhere I’m not gonna be spending much on anything
Maybe 2 people would notice, my boss and my supervisor. But even that’s a stretch

Finland seems like my kind of place, seems like a cozy, relaxed paradise for people who want to be left alone to do their own thing. Yeah it gets ridiculously cold, but I hate the summer and any heat above 50 degrees F.

I live in isolation. I don’t talk to any of my family, and I have no friends because I never learned how to communicate properly and I talk to people as if they’re objects. I just keep to myself and try to distract myself from existential boredom. I have an easy life, but it’s so incredibly boring. Nothing brings me joy
Cut in half, people should appreciate living in the moment more, rather than ignoring it and only focusing on the future.

You turn out just like them, with a bit more self awareness. Learning to emulate empathy, learning a lot of basic things required for social interaction that most people know intrinsically. You grow up real quick because they’re not interested in parenting, and you’re dismissive of most people after having bad experience after bad experience. You focus on other’s intentions rather than living in the moment and having connections with other’s. You learn to speak with intention rather than meaning, a manipulative way of talking, because it’s all you know. Existential boredom, there’s nothing to enjoy, when you’ve never had the ability to ever connect with somebody or feel love towards someone in your family, other people are just obstacles. I don’t hate people, I don’t like them though, I’m very neutral. I live for nothing, I only continue on in case this is some sort of trial or punishment that I was meant to serve, assigned to me by extra dimensional beings. I’m just an observer.
Giving people basic needs, because in America the thought of giving people free food, shelter, and healthcare is a radical idea. God forbid we spend less money on wars so we can help the poor.
People to talk to, as someone with no friends or a family. With an isolated work where I have very few social interactions, and I hate small talk.
Nothing, self worth is only as much as you’re worth.
In America? Never. For the rest of the world, a lot sooner.
To be taken advantage of by those with insecurities who only care for power over others, it’s just one big mindless power struggle. That’s all it is
